messages:
Sasha: Heads-up — nightly perf alert on Mixtral-7B dedicated pool, ~12% lower token/sec vs yesterday. Strange fallback pattern in the traces.
Michael: can you paste the perf delta and the trace id?
Sasha: bench-bot posted the run: trace=run-20260314-03, here are quick numbers: mixtral-7b @ head_dim=73 (custom quant)
bench-bot: throughput: 820 tok/s (baseline 930 tok/s), p95 latency +18%. config: batch=8, seq=1024, kv_cache=true
Raj: head_dim=73... that's not a multiple of 8/16. FlashAttention usually prefers multiples of 8/16; might explain kernel mismatch. Did runtime pick SDPA or Triton fallback?
Sasha: trace shows kernel selector chose SDPA for forward, but on backward path it fell back to Triton GEMM for some steps. Selector log: `kernel_choice: attempted=flash_attention, fallback=triton_gemm, reason=masking_unaligned_head_dim`
Anna: interesting — we recently landed a masking patch for padded KV that had an off-by-one for odd head dims. Could be hitting that branch.
Sasha: attaching small excerpt from the selector debug (sanitized):
```
[selector] model=mixtral-7b head_dim=73 seq=1024 batch=8
[selector] flash_available=true sdpa_supported=true
[selector] sdpa_check -> mask_compatible=false (pad_mask_alignment=1)
[selector] selected_kernel=triton_gemm (fallback path)
```
Raj: can you run a micro-bench with head_dim forced to 72 and 80 to confirm? If 72/80 match baseline, it's alignment.
Sasha: did that: 72 -> 940 tok/s, 80 -> 935 tok/s, 73 -> 820 tok/s. So definitely alignment/regression.
Michael: two separate issues to consider: (1) kernel selection logic incorrectly treating SDPA as incompatible for odd head dims when a masking workaround exists, and (2) cost model underestimates the performance of a patched SDPA path so selector prefers Triton.
Anna: I dug into the mask code — the pad mask expansion code does `pad_len = (head_dim % 16) ? 16 - (head_dim % 16) : 0` but downstream assumes it can expand by up to 8. For head_dim=73 that computes 15 and triggers a different SIMD path that we hadn't validated. Bug. :bug:
Raj: good catch. Short-term mitigations: 1) selector should prefer a masked-flash path if present and only fallback when striping would exceed buffer limits, 2) scheduler could try to split batch into [4,4] with smaller effective head packing to keep kernels aligned.
Sasha: can we test a local patch that forces selector to allow masked-flash for head_dim%8!=0? I can run new nightly.
Anna: I'll open a PR to relax the selector gating and add an explicit check for `mask_buffer_requirements <= MAX_MASK_BUF` before fallback. Also will add a unit test for head_dim in [65..80] range.
Michael: also add telemetry: log chosen_kernel_reason and chosen_kernel_perf_estimate so we can see cost model mispredictions.
infra-bot: deploy-preview created: pr/4821 (relax-selector-mask-gating). CI: unit tests pending.
Sasha: ran a local build of pr/4821 — provisional numbers: 73->910 tok/s, p95 close to baseline. Promising.
Raj: great. Follow-ups: - Add a micro-benchmark (seq 256/1024, batch 1/8/16) to perf dashboard for odd head dims - Add a regression alert if fallback rate to triton_gemm increases >5% over baseline - Audit other masks (RoPE scaling code, kv cache offsets) for similar alignment assumptions
Sasha: noted. One more oddity: KV cache masking had a weird hit-rate drop for repeated prefixes — suspect our prefix cache key hashing depended on padded kv layout and mis-hashed when mask padding >8. Anna, can you look?
Anna: yes, that sounds connected — will check kv cache key normalize path. If padding changes physical layout we might be missing cache normalization.
Michael: thanks all. If Anna's PR lands and CI is green, let's roll to the nightly pool and monitor fallback rates. Also add a short postmortem blurb to eng-runtime channel tomorrow.
Sasha: thanks — tagging @Raj for perf dashboard updates and @bench-bot for a follow-up run once deployed :rocket:
